title: The sparsification theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava
abstract: Let (Ω, μ) be a measure space and a = (a_k) a family of m square-integrable functions whose Gram matrix ∫ a a* dμ is the identity. Then for every n ≥ m there are points x₁, …, xₙ ∈ Ω and weights w₁, …, wₙ > 0 with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑ᵢ wᵢ a(xᵢ) a(xᵢ)* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I in the Loewner order. For the counting measure on a finite set Ω this is the theorem for finitely many vectors: if v_k ∈ ℂᵐ, k ∈ Ω, satisfy ∑_k v_k v_k* = I, then for every n ≥ m there are weights s_k ≥ 0, at most n of them nonzero, with (1 − √((m−1)/n))² I ≼ ∑_k s_k v_k v_k* ≼ (1 + √((m−1)/n))² I, so a reweighted subset of at most n of the vectors is a spectral sparsifier of their sum. The original theorem of Batson, Spielman and Srivastava has the constants (1 ∓ √(m/n))²; with m − 1 in place of m, following Chkifa, Dolbeault, Krieg and Ullrich, the statements here are slightly stronger.
